changes.text: 受降消息传到北军阵线，士兵们开始鸣放百响礼炮庆贺，格兰特立刻派人叫停：南军现在是俘虏，不该为他们的垮台而欢呼。第二天两人交谈时，李说，南方是个大国，也许要来回走三四遍，战事才能完全结束，不过对方已无力抵抗，做得到；他诚挚希望北军不必再被迫造成更多死伤和牺牲，但无法预言结果。格兰特请李出面劝全部南军投降，说以李的影响，必会被欣然接受；李说，不先征询总统，他不能那样做。

When news of the surrender reached the Union lines, the men began firing a salute of a hundred guns in honor of the victory. Grant at once sent word to have it stopped: "The Confederates were now our prisoners, and we did not want to exult over their downfall." The next day, in the course of a conversation between the two men, Lee said the South was a big country, and Union troops might have to march over it three or four times before the war entirely ended — though it could now be done, since the South could no longer resist. He earnestly hoped, however, that the Union would not be called upon to cause more loss and sacrifice of life; he could not foretell the result. Grant then suggested that no man in the Confederacy had such influence with the soldiery and the whole people as Lee, and that if he would now advise the surrender of all the armies, his advice would be followed with alacrity. Lee said he could not do that without consulting the President first.
格兰特回信说，他没有谈和的权限，南方放下武器就能让和平早日到来。此后李再次来信，可这封信送得很费劲：由于格兰特所走的路线，这封信很可能无法在约定时间内送到他手里并带回答复，除非信使穿过南军战线。因此，李派人护送带信的军官穿过自己的战线，把信送到格兰特手里。另据格兰特记述，米德和谢里登都对是否停火非常犹豫，怕这不是真心求和；而且北弗吉尼亚军团已无路可逃，除非用诡计脱身。

Grant replied that he had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and that by laying down their arms the South would hasten peace. Lee then wrote again, but this message was hard to deliver: from the route Grant had taken, it would probably not be possible to reach him and get an answer back within the time fixed unless the messenger passed through the rebel lines. Lee therefore sent an escort with the officer bearing the message through his own lines to Grant. Separately, Grant records that Meade and Sheridan both hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all. They were afraid the overture was not in good faith; and the Army of Northern Virginia was where it could not escape except by some deception.

此前两人没有一个字谈到私产、佩刀或类似问题。李看来对最初提出的条件并无异议；或者即便有意见，也想等条件写成文字再提。李读到佩刀、马匹和军官私物这一段时，说这会对他的军队有良好影响；格兰特说他讲这话时带着感情，并注明那只是自己当时的看法。至于流传甚广的李献剑、格兰特再把剑退回，格兰特把这件事以及关于它的许多其他说法直斥为“纯属虚构的传奇”：直到他把这一句写进条文，两人都没提过剑或佩刀，这不是预谋，是写到那里才想起来的。他还说，假如自己碰巧漏写、而李提了出来，他也会把这一项照样写进条款，就像他同意让士兵留下马匹那一条一样。

Not one word had passed between the two men about private property, side-arms or anything of the kind. Lee appeared to have no objection to the terms first proposed, or if he had a point against them he preferred to wait until they were in writing. When he read the passage about side-arms, horses and the officers' private property, he remarked with some feeling, Grant thought, that this would have a happy effect upon his army. As for the famous story of Lee surrendering his sword and Grant handing it back, Grant dismissed it and much else said about the occasion as "the purest romance." Until he wrote it into the terms, neither man had mentioned sword or side-arms. There was no premeditation: the thought did not occur to him until the moment he set it down. Had he happened to omit it and Lee called his attention to it, he said, he would have put it in precisely as he acceded to the provision about the soldiers keeping their horses.

dispositions.rationale: 中文改为“士兵们开始鸣放百响礼炮庆贺，格兰特立刻派人叫停”，不再暗示百响已经鸣完，与原文和英文 began firing 一致。英文原本与证据相符，未作改动，按同步规则给出全文。

evidence.quote: our men commenced firing a salute of a hundred guns in honor of the victory. I at once sent word, however, to have it stopped

dispositions.rationale: 把米德与谢里登犹豫的句子移出送信叙事，放到段末单独成句，并以“另据格兰特记述”或 Separately, Grant records 引出，不再暗示时间先后或因果关系。李派卫队护送一事保留“因此”，因为原文的 therefore 指向路线问题。

evidence.quote: both of these commanders hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all
Lee, therefore, sent an escort with the officer bearing this message through his lines to me

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上“以及关于它的许多其他说法”，与英文 and much else said about the occasion 一致。同时按规则4，中文正文不嵌入英文，把原来的「the purest romance」改为现代汉语转述“纯属虚构的传奇”，并改用“”。英文未改动，按同步规则给出全文。

evidence.quote: this and much more that has been said about it is the purest romance
